chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Rafa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the one in Ihram wearing the two khuff (leather socks) and the two jawaban (socks). He said: 'When he is in need of them.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram wear socks or leather footwear?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *al-idtirar* (necessity) within the strict prohibitions of Ihram, allowing the wearing of leather socks (*khuffayn*) and socks (*jawbayn*) when bare feet are not feasible. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on practical ease (*rukhas*) within ritual purity, ensuring that the pilgrim is not burdened by conditions that make the standard prohibition of bare feet impractical or harmful.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Rafa’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam wearing the two shoes and the two socks. Heasws said: ‘When he is desperate for these two’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Rifa’ah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who in the state of Ihram wears shoes and socks. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can do so in case it is an emergency. ‘“
